newsitem.title: USA: Mercer Cty, N.J., agency in deal on Oct 1 payment.
newsitem.headline: Mercer Cty, N.J., agency in deal on Oct 1 payment.

text.p: The Mercer County Improvement Authority, N.J., plans to use proceeds from a private placement to pay a $5.8 million interest payment due Oct 1 on a 1992 bond issue, according to Moody's Investors Service Inc.

In a statement on the credit to be published Friday, Moody's said it has placed all its ratings for the agency's various debt under review, pending discussions with the county, the authority and project representatives.

Construction of the agency's waste-to-energy facility, for which the 1992 bonds were sold, has been on hold because of legal uncertainties. In 1995, the U.S. Third Court of Appeals overturned a lower court ruling which had upheld New Jersey's system of regulating flow control systems.
Another legal challenge project came from a lawsuit arguing the the county must refile its construction plans because it significantly amended its original plans since they were first approved.

A ruling on that case is pending, and "may have a significant impact on the timing and configuration of the resource recovery project and on the ability of the project sponsors to deliver the facility as planned," Moody's said.
